attribution.title: Walter Sisulu Nasionale Botaniese Tuin, uitsig a
attribution.author: JMK
attribution.description: Northeastward view over the Walter Sisulu National Botanical Garden in western Roodepoort, Gauteng, showing the vicinity of the reception area and the sprawling lawns flanking the footpaths. The footpath (leading diagonally over the scene) converges on Muldersdrift se Loop, the watercourse that bisects the gardens. Beyond the upper footbridge (out of view) this footpath arrives at the large lawn flanking the plunge pool of the waterfall over the Roodekrans. From the plunge pool, a visitor can take the Geological Trail, a very steep footpath to the top of the waterfall and the natural bankenveld vegetation beyond.

attribution.title: 'The Cave' - Melville Koppies Nature Reserve
attribution.author: The Heritage Portal
attribution.description:
A father and son visit the Melville Koppies Cave. The Blue Plaque for the site reads as follows:
"The cave is a fissure formed between 2.9 billion-year-old quartzite rocks of what is now the Melville Koppies Ridge. For hundreds of years the cave provided a shelter for people living around and moving across the area. The site was excavated in 1971. An analysis of the archaeological remains found in the cave suggests that, as early as 1500 A.D., farming communities made use of the resources the area had to offer. When supplies dwindled they supplemented their diet with wild plants and hunted wild animals."
